written_derivation_front: Let eta be mu_E minus mu_O on their disjoint transported-band supports, and theta_i=eta_i/[e(t_i)o(t_i)]. SE/SO imply theta annihilates o*P3 and e*P3. Since e,o are coprime cubics, that sum is ALL P6: its only pair kernel is the scalar pair(e,-o), so dimension is8-1=7.

Consequently a nonzero theta requires at least8 DISTINCT active frequencies and at least7 sign changes; otherwise Lagrange isolation or a polynomial of degree<=6 matching its sign runs contradicts its vanishing moments.

Within EACH of the six ordered transported hulls, theta has positive sign to the LEFT of that hull's selected root and negative sign to its RIGHT, for BOTH parities. This follows from eta's opposite E/O signs and interlacing of e,o. There is at most one internal sign change per active hull.

If r is the number of nonempty active hulls and B the number with active frequencies on BOTH sides of their selected root, the total sign changes are at most(r-1)+B. Hence r+B>=8, r>=4 and B>=2. Every two-sided active hull has its selected root in the INTERIOR of its actual own root band; a root outside the band can mismatch actual roots only on one side.

Thus any stationary transport must exhibit at least8 active frequencies and at least2 two-sided equioscillating bands. A single active frequency in each of six hulls cannot be a full stationary point. This local-root consequence is a written next-front derivation, not a newly reviewed theorem or a contradiction to the known critical8-node alternatives.
